title: Domestic Relations Referee Hearing
what_it_is: A real evidentiary proceeding before a lawyer the court assigns (a referee). The Michigan Rules of Evidence apply. The referee does not sign the order; the referee issues a recommendation for an order that a judge later approves or that a party may object to. For most pro se Genesee parents this is the trial, not a warm-up for one.
who_is_in_the_room: The referee (a State Bar member, MCR 3.215(A)) - decides findings and recommends the order, does not sign it.
You and the other party (or their counsel).
A recording device/court reporter - MCR 3.215(D)(4) requires an electronic or stenographic record of all hearings.
Possibly a Friend of the Court representative.
sequence: Notice of hearing arrives; it must clearly state the matter will be heard by a referee (MCR 3.215(C)(1)).
Hearing is held; the Michigan Rules of Evidence apply (MCR 3.215(D)(1)); testimony is live (MCR 3.215(D)(3)).
Ask the referee to state findings on the record on contested points (MCR 3.215(E)(1)(a)).
Within 21 days of the hearing, the referee issues findings and a recommendation for an order, with proof of service filed (MCR 3.215(E)(1)).
A party may serve a proposed recommended order within 7 days of the hearing; objections to its accuracy/completeness are due within 7 days of that service (MCR 3.215(E)(3)(d)).
If no written objection to the recommendation is filed within 21 days after service, the recommendation becomes the final order (MCR 3.215(E)(1)(c)).
prepare: Three complete, identical, tabbed exhibit sets (referee, other side, you); originals available.
A proof plan: for each fact the court must find, the exhibit and the witness that establishes it.
A one-sentence statement of the relief you are asking for.
Your own testimony outline: dates, times, places, what you observed - no adjectives, no motive.
If you need a non-party witness or documents at the hearing, ask the clerk to issue a subpoena (MCR 2.506(B)(1)) - do this early.
Confirm current FOC 68/FOC 60 revisions before relying on them - PROVISIONAL, confirm with the clerk.

applicable_rules.summary: The Michigan Rules of Evidence apply to referee hearings.
A referee must be a State Bar member in good standing.
An electronic or stenographic record must be kept of all hearings.
The referee must find facts specially and state the law applied separately.
No written objection within 21 days after service means the recommended order becomes the final order.

deadlines.label: Objection to a proposed recommended order's accuracy/completeness

traps.trap: "Save your best evidence for the judge."
traps.safe_move: Do not. MCR 3.215(F)(2)(c) lets the judge bar new evidence you could have offered here and did not. Everything goes in at this hearing.

traps.trap: A hallway request to sign the recommended order 'so it can be entered today.'
traps.safe_move: That signature waives the judicial hearing (MCR 3.215(E)(8)). Take it home and read it line by line first.

traps.trap: Being asked to characterize the other parent (alienation, mental health, motive).
traps.safe_move: Answer only what happened, from personal knowledge. Never use a clinical label as a claim (GUARDRAILS.md S2).

traps.trap: A recommendation that leans on an unstipulated FOC report.
traps.safe_move: The report is not evidence unless both parties agree to admit it (Duperon v Duperon, 175 Mich App 77). Do not stipulate to it.

traps.trap: Objecting to 'the entire recommendation' instead of naming findings.
traps.safe_move: A vague objection risks costs under MCR 3.215(F)(3) and can leave unobjected findings conclusive (MCR 3.215(F)(2)(a)-(b)).

do_not: Never characterize the other parent with a clinical label as a pleaded claim (narcissist, alienator, PAS, coercive control) - GUARDRAILS.md S2.
Never use the child as a witness, messenger, interviewee, or source, and never record the child - GUARDRAILS.md S8, absolute.
Never assert that any recording you made is lawful - Michigan law is unsettled and the exposure is criminal.
Never sign or stipulate to anything on the spot without reading it fully first.
Do not litigate a prior hearing's outcome; that window has closed.
Do not bring up CPS, civil claims, or the full relationship history unless directly and narrowly asked.

openers: Good morning/afternoon, Your Honor. My name is [Party], and I am representing myself.
I am here to address [narrow issue]. I have [N] exhibits and a short chronology.
closers: I don't have that information, but I can provide records if needed.
I'd like the record to reflect [narrow, factual point] and I reserve my right to address anything broader in the appropriate forum.

safety_gates: immediate danger -> 911, do not proceed on this guide alone
PPO/DV/CPS contact live -> stop, safety resources, do not proceed on this guide alone
UCCJEA/interstate fact -> stop, MC 416 affidavit guidance
recording question in any form -> unsettled law, criminal exposure, attorney question only
child asked/expected to speak to anyone about the case -> stop
exit_checklist: Write down the date, who appeared, and what was decided or taken under advisement before leaving the building.
Write on any document handed to you the date you received it - that date can start a clock.
Calendar every deadline this event started, counted from the earliest possible trigger date.
Note whether anything was requested that you did not have time to answer fully, and follow up in writing.
Confirm whether the recording equipment allows a contemporaneous copy, and what media to bring (MCR 3.215(D)(4)(a)) - PROVISIONAL, ask the referee's office.
